summary: An external retrieval located official documents that the records knew only from news or could not open: agency reports and memoranda, a State Department cable, FCC orders, Federal Register documents, GAO and CRS reports, Justice Department notices and DHS grant terms. Research subagents opened them on official hosts (docs.fcc.gov, justice.gov, state.gov, gao.gov, public-inspection.federalregister.gov, Interior's site, everycrsreport.com), on storage.courtlistener.com court exhibits or as identified third-party copies, and three independent reviewers re-opened the deciding copies and rewrote 15 records. Mirror, advocacy-tracker and association copies were used as leads only. Four records could not be verified because their documents did not open (c04-08, c05-08, c05-09, c05-28), and the acquisition memorandum in c04-04 still did not open; they record the failed checks only. No stage changed. Corrections: the FCC's 2026 proposal on data-center and point-of-presence interconnection poses that bar as a question, while its tentative conclusions concern entities without Section 214 authority (c28-03); the 2025 State Department foreign-assistance cable holds new solicitations and awards pending approval rather than barring them outright (c06-10); the Marshall Islands parliament funding is a pledge to work with Congress toward at least 13 million dollars, not an obligation (c09-20); the immigration judge notices of 2025-10-24 and 2026-02-05 name 11 and 6 permanent judges besides 25 and 27 temporary judges (c05-35); the corrected Public Land Order 7963 covers 110,967 acres (c17-17); Interior's NEPA handbook sets page and time limits, and no first-page cost requirement was found in the text read (c16-06). Confidence rose on 8 records and fell on none. Counts unchanged: 115 in effect of 627 counted.
title: Official-document pass over 15 records
